period.note_en: The Quran gives no date or era in years for Yusuf; the king and the years it mentions are not dated.

region.text_en: He was taken to Egypt, where the man who bought him gave him a place to stay; later he told his parents to enter Egypt, and God says He established him in the land.

community.text_en: He was a son of Yaqub and followed the way of his forefathers Ibrahim, Ishaq and Yaqub, not associating anything with God.

lifespan.note_en: The Quran gives no age for Yusuf. It says he reached full strength, spent several years in prison, and later died.

daily_activities.text_en: In prison two young men asked him to interpret their dreams; he did so and called them to worship God alone. Later he supplied provisions to those who came to him for supplies.

occupation.text_en: God gave him judgement and knowledge; he asked to be set over the storehouses of the land as a knowing guardian, and the king told him he was established and trusted.

foods_beverages.text_en: He spoke of the food provided to his prison companions; in his plan for the years of plenty, the harvest was left in its ear except a little for eating, so that stored grain served the hard years.

farming_livestock.text_en: He advised that people sow for seven years continuously and leave what they harvested in its ear, saving only a little for eating.

clothing_care.text_en: His shirt is mentioned three times: his brothers brought it with false blood on it, it was torn from behind in the household, and it was later cast over his father's face.

housing.text_en: In Egypt he was given an honourable place to stay in the house of the man who bought him, later spent years in prison, and when established could settle wherever he wished in the land.

transport.text_en: A caravan came to the well and its people took him and sold him; the Quran also mentions a camel's load as a measure of supplies, and a caravan setting out with his shirt.

family_community.text_en: His father warned him not to tell his dream to his brothers, who plotted against him; later he told his brother who he was, forgave the others, and raised his parents on the throne.

customs_leisure.text_en: His brothers asked to take him out to enjoy himself and play; later he called himself the best of hosts, giving full measure to those who came for supplies.

education.text_en: God taught him the interpretation of events and gave him judgement and knowledge; he said his understanding came from what his Lord had taught him.

health_treatment.text_en: The Quran mentions no illness of Yusuf. It says his father's eyes turned white from grief, and that sight returned when Yusuf's shirt was cast on his father's face.

climate.text_en: His interpretation foretold seven years of sowing, then seven hard years that would consume the stored grain, then a year of relief. The Quran gives no other description of the weather.

worship.text_en: He told his prison companions that judgement belongs to God alone and that they should worship none but Him, and he prayed to be taken as one who submits and joined with the righteous.

challenges.text_en: His brothers put him in the bottom of a well, he was sold for a few dirhams, tempted in the household and imprisoned for several years; he asked his Lord to turn plotting away from him.

differences_modern.text_en: Educational interpretation (not scripture): the Quran gives the stages of Yusuf's life as events with their meaning, but no dates, names of rulers or measurements of places, so these should not be added from outside sources as if the Quran stated them.

lessons.text_en: Educational interpretation (not scripture): these passages present refusing wrongdoing even at the cost of prison, and forgiving his brothers, when he said there was no blame on them that day, as marks of how Yusuf met hardship.
